key_evidence: For 26 years the City of Dayton required a permit to distribute food, clothing or toiletries in a public place in the central area of the city, with a $50 fee per event and a $250 security deposit for organisations with prior violations.

On 7 April 2024 a Dayton police officer handcuffed and detained Nourish Our Neighbors volunteer Mitchell West for more than 30 minutes after he handed a burrito to a homeless man in Courthouse Square. No charges were brought.
In June 2026 Judge Thomas Rose of the US District Court for the Southern District of Ohio held the ordinance unconstitutional under the First Amendment and barred Dayton from enforcing it.

The City of Dayton appealed that ruling, then dropped the appeal and had its city commission approve a settlement of $56,365.62 in September 2026. The money covers the nonprofit’s attorney fees and costs only.
The City of Dayton declined to comment on the settlement and made no acknowledgment of harm at any stage — not before the ruling, not after it, and not on settling.
Nothing in the settlement reaches Mitchell West, who was handcuffed, or the homeless people who went unfed during the two years the case ran.
No source located shows the city commission has repealed the ordinance; a court has only barred its enforcement.

ATTRIBUTION IS CLEAN: the ordinance, the arresting officer, the appeal and the settlement are all City of Dayton acts. Unlike San Francisco (federal ICE conduct) and Copenhagen (national police conduct) in the same cycle, there is no misattribution risk here.

dimension_rationale.EMP: raw 2.5 to 2.2. One subdimension moves: E4 Validation 3 to 2. A court established the harm; the city appealed, settled and declined to comment. No validation of the harmed party at any point and no process for it. The other four EMP subdimensions hold at the integer-grid expansion of the published 2.5.
dimension_rationale.EQU: raw 2.0 to 1.8. One subdimension moves: EQ4 Access Design 2 to 1. The city did not merely fail to identify an access barrier; it created one, priced it at $50 per event, arrested a volunteer for crossing it, and litigated to keep it. Anchor 1 is the closest match and understates the finding.
dimension_rationale.ACC: raw 2.5 to 1.6, the largest move. Three subdimensions move: AB1 Harm Acknowledgment 3 to 1 (anchor 2 requires harm acknowledged after external establishment; here it was externally established by a federal judge and still not acknowledged — the city appealed, then declined to comment); AB2 Correction Willingness 3 to 2 (court-compelled and incomplete, with no located repeal); AB5 Reparative Action 2 to 1 (the $56,365.62 covers attorney fees and costs only — anchor 1 verbatim). AB1’s starting value of 3 was itself a placeholder grid expansion, so this is a first assessment landing on anchor 1 rather than a two-step drop from an assessed value.
dimension_rationale.unchanged: AWR, ACT, BND, SYS and INT move only by integer-grid rounding of the published 2.5 to 2.4, with no evidence move. They do not require proposed_subdimensions and will be reconstructed from index values at apply time.

screening_checks.directionality: PASS. Dayton surfaced on negative evidence and this is a downgrade. No upward move was made anywhere. The city’s only positive act — paying the settlement — reimbursed opposing counsel rather than repairing anyone harmed, so it supports no upward move.
screening_checks.rationale_vs_history: PASS. No documented history contradicts this rationale; there is no prior Dayton assessment or applied change to contradict.
screening_checks.not_a_calibration_proposal: PASS. Three dimensions move on five specifically evidenced subdimensions. Five dimensions are held at grid rounding. The seed-placeholder and 35.9-cohort observations are filed as a calibration_flag, not as the basis of the move.
screening_checks.sourcing_bar: Filed on the magnitude trigger, not a band crossing, so the band-crossing bar (two distinct sources, at least one at tier 4 or better) does not apply. Four distinct sources support the moves (WYSO tier 2, Dayton Daily News tier 2, Pacific Legal Foundation case page and press release tier 1, plus Journal-News and Bloomberg Law tier 2 corroboration). No tier 4 or better source is in hand because the federal court order itself was not obtained — confidence is set to medium for that reason.
screening_checks.conflict_of_interest: None. Two of five evidence items come from Pacific Legal Foundation, the plaintiff’s own counsel and therefore an interested party, and are labelled as such. Their factual claims used here (arrest date, detention length, ruling holding) are corroborated independently by WYSO and the Dayton Daily News.
